1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. CDK: Cloud Development Kit; SAM: Serverless Application Model; CI: continuous integration; CD: continuous delivery; ETL: extract, transform, load; SDK: software development kit; RDS: Relational Database Service; EFS: Elastic File System; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; DAG: directed acyclic graph; EMR: Elastic MapReduce; CLI: command line interface; YAML: YAML Ain't Markup Language; IAM: Identity and Access Management; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; ECS: Elastic Container Service; HDFS: Hadoop Distributed File System; MSK: Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka; SQS: Simple Queue Service; MWAA: Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow

  • Optimize code to cut runtime in ingestion and transformation
  • Configure Lambda for concurrency, memory, storage and performance
  • Pick languages and frameworks for data engineering
  • Apply software engineering practices: version control, testing, logging, monitoring
  • Deploy with infrastructure as code: CloudFormation, CDK and AWS SAM
  • Describe CI/CD for data pipelines, distributed computing, and data structures and algorithms

The exam does not test language syntax: it tests which tool, setting or practice fits a situation.

2Optimizing Code and Runtime (skill 1.4.1)

Running case

Kestrel Freight Speeds Up Its Nightly Job

  • The nightly transform takes six hours and the window is four
  • It loops over rows one by one, calls an API per record and writes thousands of tiny files
  • Your job: make it fit the window without more servers
Problem Fix
Row-by-row loops Vectorized or set-based operations (SQL, DataFrames) instead of per-record code
Reading too much data Filter early (push-down predicates), read only needed columns, partition pruning, columnar formats
Expensive shuffles Broadcast the small side of a join, filter before joining, partition on the join key
Repeated work Cache reused data; do expensive setup once (see Lambda init code below)
One call per record Batch requests (BatchWriteItem, PutRecords, bulk COPY), reuse connections
Tiny output files Coalesce or compact to larger files
Sequential work that is independent Parallelize (more partitions, workers, concurrent tasks)
Guessing Measure first: CloudWatch metrics, Spark UI, profilers
Exam tip

The fix for slow ETL is usually less data read, set-based processing, parallelism, and fewer larger files, not a bigger instance by default.

3Lambda Concurrency and Performance (skill 1.4.2)

Setting What it does
Memory (128 MB to 10,240 MB) Also sets CPU share: more memory means more CPU and often a faster, sometimes cheaper run
Timeout Up to 15 minutes per invocation
Reserved concurrency Guarantees and caps a function's concurrent executions: protects critical functions and limits load on a downstream database; no extra charge; setting 0 stops the function
Provisioned concurrency Pre-initialized environments to remove cold starts; extra charge; helps interactive (latency-sensitive) workloads, rarely needed for pipelines
Account concurrency Default 1,000 concurrent executions per Region (can be raised); you can reserve up to the unreserved amount minus 100
Ephemeral storage (/tmp) 512 MB to 10,240 MB, per execution environment, encrypted at rest: scratch space for ETL, large objects, models
Event source mapping Batch size, batching window, parallelization factor, error handling for streams and queues (Module 2)
Architecture Arm (Graviton) often cheaper and faster than x86 for the same work
  • Estimate concurrency = average requests per second × average duration in seconds
  • Init code outside the handler (SDK clients, database connections, loaded models) runs once per environment and is reused, which reduces latency and cost
  • Databases: many concurrent functions open many connections: limit with reserved concurrency or use RDS Proxy to pool them
  • Failure handling: destinations or a dead-letter queue for asynchronous invocations
  • Layers package shared libraries; container images (up to 10 GB) hold large dependencies

Mounting storage in Lambda (skill 1.4.7) [Verify live]

  • /tmp ephemeral storage: temporary, per execution environment
  • Amazon EFS: mount a shared, persistent file system (the function must be in a VPC; use an access point; path such as /mnt/data): for large shared files, libraries or models
  • Amazon S3 Files: a newer option that mounts an S3 bucket as a file system (a function uses either EFS or S3 Files, not both)
  • Do not mount to store results you need forever: write to S3 or a database
Exam tip

"Lambda must read a large shared model or reference file on every invocation" → mount Amazon EFS (or load once into /tmp at init). "A function overloads the database with connections" → reserved concurrency and RDS Proxy.

4Languages, Frameworks and Engineering Practices (skills 1.4.3 and 1.4.4)

Languages and frameworks

Language Typical data-engineering use
Python PySpark and Glue scripts, boto3 (AWS SDK), pandas, Lambda, Airflow DAGs
SQL Athena, Redshift, Spark SQL, transformations and views: the common language of data
Scala Native language of Apache Spark; Glue and EMR jobs
Java Kafka and Flink applications, Lambda, Hadoop
R Statistics and analysis (EMR, SageMaker notebooks)
Bash / PowerShell Scripting and automation (AWS CLI, AWS Tools for PowerShell)

Practices

Practice In data engineering
Version control (Git) All code and infrastructure templates in Git; branches, pull requests, reviews
Testing Unit tests for functions, integration tests on sample data, data tests (row counts, nulls, schema), regression checks
Logging Structured logs with job, run and record identifiers; send to CloudWatch Logs
Monitoring Metrics and alarms on runtime, failures, lag, data volume
Configuration and secrets Parameters outside the code; secrets in Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store
Environments Separate dev, test and prod with the same templates
Modularity and idempotency Small reusable functions; re-runnable jobs
Exam tip

"Make the pipeline repeatable and reviewable" → Git for code and IaC templates plus automated tests in a pipeline.

5Infrastructure as Code (skills 1.4.5, 1.4.6 and 1.4.8)

Tool What it is Pick it when
AWS CloudFormation Declarative templates (YAML or JSON) that create a stack of resources You need repeatable, reviewable infrastructure for any AWS resource
AWS CDK (Cloud Development Kit) Define infrastructure in a programming language (Python, TypeScript, Java and more); it synthesizes to CloudFormation You want loops, functions, classes and reuse (constructs) for infrastructure
AWS SAM (Serverless Application Model) Shorthand extension of CloudFormation for serverless (Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31) plus the SAM CLI Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, Step Functions pipelines

CloudFormation essentials

  • A template describes resources; a stack is the deployed instance; change sets preview updates; drift detection finds manual changes; StackSets deploy to many accounts and Regions
  • Deployments are repeatable: the same template builds dev, test and prod
  • Rollback on failure keeps the stack consistent

AWS SAM essentials (skill 1.4.6)

  • Resource types: AWS::Serverless::Function, ::Api, ::HttpApi, ::SimpleTable (DynamoDB), ::StateMachine (Step Functions) and more, expanded to CloudFormation at deploy time
  • SAM CLI: sam init, sam build, sam local invoke (test locally), sam deploy, sam sync (fast sync of local changes)
  • Connectors generate the IAM permissions between resources
Exam tip

"Package and deploy a Lambda + Step Functions + DynamoDB pipeline with the least template code" → AWS SAM. "Define infrastructure with a programming language" → AWS CDK. "Repeatable deployment of any resources from a template" → CloudFormation.

6CI/CD for Data Pipelines (skill 1.4.9)

  • Continuous integration (CI): every change is built and tested automatically (unit tests, data tests, template validation)
  • Continuous delivery or deployment (CD): tested changes are released automatically (delivery may add a manual approval before production)
  • AWS services: AWS CodePipeline (orchestrates the stages), AWS CodeBuild (builds and runs tests), AWS CodeDeploy (deploys to Lambda, EC2, ECS with canary, linear or all-at-once shifts and rollback), CloudFormation (deploys the infrastructure)
  • Source: Git hosts such as GitHub or GitLab, S3 or ECR (AWS CodeCommit is no longer on the in-scope list)
  • Data-pipeline specifics: test transformations on a small sample dataset, deploy Glue scripts to S3 and update job definitions, promote the same artifact from test to production, roll back with the previous version
Exam tip

"Automatically test and deploy changes to Glue jobs and Step Functions on every commit" → CodePipeline with CodeBuild (tests) and CloudFormation or SAM (deploy).

7Distributed Computing and Data Structures (skills 1.4.10 and 1.4.11)

Distributed computing

  • Distributed computing splits data and work across many machines that cooperate, so a job scales out beyond one machine and tolerates node failures
  • Spark: a driver plans the job; executors run tasks on partitions of the data; a shuffle moves data between executors (expensive); lazy evaluation builds a plan first
  • MapReduce idea: map (process pieces in parallel) then reduce (combine); HDFS stores blocks across nodes
  • Trade-offs: scale out (more nodes) versus scale up (bigger node); data locality; network cost of shuffles; skew
  • Services: EMR, Glue (Spark), Athena, Redshift (MPP), Kinesis shards, MSK partitions

Data structures and algorithms

Structure What it is Where you meet it
Graph Nodes joined by edges (directed or not, loops allowed) Amazon Neptune (graph database), data lineage, pipeline dependencies (DAGs), relationships (customers and shipments)
Tree A graph with a root, parents and children and no cycles Hierarchies (organization, categories), B-tree indexes in databases, partition prefixes
Hash table Key → value by a hash function Partition keys (DynamoDB, Kinesis, Kafka), hash joins
Queue / stack First in first out / last in first out SQS, buffering streams
Sorted structures Ordered data enables binary search Sort keys, sorted columnar files
  • Traversal visits nodes: breadth-first (level by level) and depth-first (follow a path deep first); shortest path finds the cheapest route between nodes
  • Complexity (Big O) describes how work grows with data size: O(1) constant (hash lookup), O(log n) (index or binary search), O(n) (full scan), O(n log n) (sorting): indexes and partitioning turn scans into lookups
Exam tip

"Model highly connected data (who is related to whom, lineage, recommendations)" → a graph and Amazon Neptune. "Look up by key fast at any size" → a hash-partitioned store such as DynamoDB.

8Exam Q&A

8.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1A nightly transformation loops over millions of rows and calls an external API once per row, so it misses its window. Which change helps MOST?

  • AMove the job to one larger single server with more memory and cores
  • BAdd more logging statements so that the slow steps become visible
  • CDisable retries on the API calls so that failures return faster
  • DBatch the API calls and replace row-by-row loops with set-based, parallel processing
Show the answer

Answer: D. Batching calls and using set-based parallel processing removes per-record overhead. A bigger server does not remove the serial work.

S2A Lambda function reading from a stream overwhelms a relational database with connections during spikes. Which TWO actions reduce the problem? (Select TWO.)

  • APlace Amazon RDS Proxy between the function and the database
  • BIncrease the function's memory to the maximum
  • CRemove the function's timeout
  • DUse provisioned concurrency to add more environments
  • ESet reserved concurrency on the function to cap parallel executions
Show the answer

Answer: A, E. Reserved concurrency limits how many functions run at once, and RDS Proxy pools connections. More memory or provisioned concurrency does not reduce connections.

S3A team wants to define a pipeline made of Lambda functions, a Step Functions state machine and a DynamoDB table with the least template code, and test the functions locally. Which tool should they use?

  • AManually created console resources
  • BAWS Glue workflows
  • CAWS SAM
  • DAmazon MWAA
Show the answer

Answer: C. AWS SAM is a CloudFormation extension with shorthand for serverless resources and a CLI for local testing and deployment.

S4Developers want to define cloud infrastructure using loops and reusable classes in Python, and still deploy through CloudFormation. Which tool fits?

  • AAWS CLI scripts only
  • BAmazon EventBridge
  • CAWS Config
  • DAWS CDK
Show the answer

Answer: D. The AWS CDK lets you define infrastructure in a programming language and synthesizes CloudFormation templates.

S5A Lambda function must load a 3 GB reference file on every invocation and share it across many functions. Which approach is BEST?

  • APackage the file in every deployment zip of every function that needs it
  • BMount an Amazon EFS file system, with the function in a VPC
  • CSend the file in each event payload from the caller
  • DStore the file in the function's environment variables
Show the answer

Answer: B. EFS provides a shared, persistent file system that Lambda can mount; deployment packages and event payloads have size limits.

S6An analyst needs to represent customers, shipments and the relationships between them for queries such as "which customers share a delivery address?" Which data structure and service fit best?

  • AA hash table in Amazon ElastiCache
  • BA graph in Amazon Neptune
  • CA queue in Amazon SQS
  • DA columnar file in Amazon S3
Show the answer

Answer: B. Highly connected data is modeled as a graph, and Amazon Neptune is the managed graph database.

9Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Optimize code Set-based, parallel, push-down filters, columnar, batch calls, fewer larger files, measure first
Lambda 128–10,240 MB memory (CPU scales); 15 min; reserved (cap and guarantee, free) vs provisioned (no cold start, charged); default 1,000 concurrent; /tmp 512–10,240 MB; EFS (or S3 Files) mount; init code outside handler
Languages Python, SQL, Scala (Spark), Java (Kafka/Flink), R, Bash, PowerShell
Practices Git, tests (unit, integration, data), logging, monitoring, secrets outside code, dev/test/prod
IaC CloudFormation (templates, stacks, change sets, drift), CDK (code → CloudFormation), SAM (serverless shorthand, sam build/deploy/local)
CI/CD CodePipeline orchestrates, CodeBuild tests, CodeDeploy releases (canary/linear), CloudFormation/SAM deploys
Distributed computing Split data and work across nodes; Spark driver/executors/partitions/shuffle; scale out; skew
Structures Graph (Neptune, lineage, DAGs), tree (hierarchies, B-trees), hash (partition keys), queue (SQS); Big O: indexes turn O(n) scans into O(log n) lookups
